paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The gospel is not advice, and it's not a nice feeling. It's news about something that happened: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day, all "according to the Scriptures" (1 Corinthians 15:3-4). Paul calls that "of first importance," so it goes at the TOP of the list, baker, above everything else.

And Paul doesn't ask the Corinthians to take it on faith with nothing behind it. He points to people who saw the risen Christ, including more than five hundred at once, most of them still living when he writes (1 Corinthians 15:5-6). He says this gospel saves, "if you hold firmly to the word I preached" (1 Corinthians 15:2). So hold on to it, baker. Don't let it slip out of your hands like a warm cookie off a spatula.

Then Paul shows what the gospel does to a person. He calls himself the least of the apostles because he persecuted the church of God (1 Corinthians 15:9). Yet he says, "by the grace of God I am what I am" (1 Corinthians 15:10). I know a little about being put away and left in the dark, friend, and I can tell you that nobody sharpens their own edges. If grace can do that for Paul, it can do it for you, so stand firm in it and keep your oven warm.
